Hmm, so the main issue here is whether it's right or wrong to ask someone not to sit on their new couch because of their weight. On one hand, the couch is their property, and they have the right to protect it. On the other hand, the family member's weight is a sensitive topic, and asking them not to sit might come off as offensive or discriminative. I should consider the intent behind the action. Or perhaps getting a more durable couch if they know the family member will be visiting often. I think the key here is balancing property protection with sensitivity. While it's reasonable to want to protect new furniture, the way it's communicated matters a lot. The person did it privately, which is good, but the underlying message might still be hurtful. So, considering all this, I'm leaning towards the person being a bit in the wrong, not because of the request itself, but because of how it might affect the family member's feelings.
